Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Rajan Roy,J.
Hon'ble Rajeev Singh,J.
Heard.
By means of this petition, the petitioner has sought quashing of F.I.R. dated 13.02.2024 bearing
Case Crime No. 45 of 2024 for the offence under Sections 376-D, 343, 506 I.P.C. registered at Police
Station- Thangaon, District- Sitapur.
The petitioner's counsel contends that the informant-victim has earlier married twice and she married the petitioner for the third time.

He has invited our attention to Annexure Nos. 2 & 3, which are documents, which according to him established marriage between the petitioner and the Virendra Kumar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Home Deptt. ...

His submission is that the F.I.R. is concocted one.

He further submits that if at all it is the second husband, namely, Ramu who could have filed any complaint or F.I.R. as the case may be against the petitioner, the F.I.R., therefore, needs to be quashed.
Learned A.G.A. has opposed the Writ Petition.
He has submitted that there is no way that Section 198 Cr.P.C. would be attracted in this situation.
There are allegations of kidnapping, rape by the informant-victim against the petitioner and other accused.
The informant has nowhere stated that she has married the petitioner.
Therefore, this plea of the petitioner that there is a marital relationship between him and the informant-victim cannot be gone into in these proceedings under Article 226 of the Constitution.
Considering the seriousness of the offence, it is not a case for quashing of the F.I.R.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the records, specially the recitals in the F.I.R. by no stretch of imagination can we say at this stage that no cognizable offence is made out.
There are allegations against the petitioner and other accused of having forcibly taken away the victim and then committed rape repeatedly for months.

In this scenario, we fail to understand that what is the relevance of Section 198 Cr.P.C.
The plea of marriage being set up by the petitioner cannot be determined in proceedings under Article 226 of the Constitution as the informant has not stated about it in her F.I.R.
We are not inclined to quash this F.I.R.
The petitioner may avail other remedies as far as permissible in law subject to cost.

Accordingly, the Writ Petition is dismissed.
.
[Rajeev Singh, J.] [Rajan Roy, J.]
